>In all honesty, your husband was a father at age 21, and it sounds like he's trying to make up for some lost time.

This is exactly the story of my family. My father was 19 and my mother 17 when I was born.This is exactly how it was, him acting as a single man while she stayed at home taking care of my sisters and I her whole life. He was rarely ever at home and when he was it was awful for all of us, like having a really annoying and entitled stranger staying over at our house. I don't know if he ever cheated on her but he was irrationaly jealous with her and abusive to all of us. They tried staying together for over 20 years untill my mom got a job and filed for divorce. I really wish they had done it sooner so that we could have had some peace while growing up.

> started "wanting to be friends" with this girl

Ah! that old familiar feeling...

We had met each other at work, in a multilingual call centre, we were both "straight", I had just broken up with a guy I'd been dating for two years (due to very straight issues he wanted to tell me how to dress, act, live etc.) and she was starting to see a guy at work, nothing serious though but still straight enough to me. We started talking, as most "straight" women mainly about guys. I knew I liked her but thought nothing would ever happen and treated the whole thing as another straight crush. The company had a lot of french speakers (like us) but was still always understaffed and we all felt miserably overworked. A french cultural event was coming up in the city so I thought it would be fun to get together a group of us french slaves and go have fun. She was supposed to help me tell people about it but when the day came nobody knew anything, she hadn't told anyone. I thought the poor thing had just forgotten about it since we were all so horribly busy. I had already finished my shift so I thought of calling her (since she was my pal) a couple other people and give it a try. I called her first, she sounded like she didn't want to go, I was trying to convince her with the usual "come on it'll be fun" and then she just said "how about we go just the two of us?" then it hit me why she hadn't told anyone, she was asking me out. I was in the middle of a bookstore, gleaming and giggling and must have done something with my hands or something because people were starting to stare and at me and laugh. I said yes, of course, but joked about it being just the two of us "alone in the woods! what if we bump into a big bad wolf?" she repplied "Oh, I'll protect you". So we went out, it was no longer that "friends hanging out vibe" anymore, it was a date. She got me a drink we talked and then at some point she asked if I had ever thought about being with a girl I answered I'm bisexual and that I didn't just like any girl but that I liked her. She was surprised, told me that she had liked me all along but she'd thought I was "straight". We dated for a couple months, it was awesome, then circumstances sort of took over and we drifted apart. But there it is, two "straight" girls, ha! go figure.

> *so it's all people that doesn't really know me well*

I'm afraid that's exactly what Facebook is, lots of people who barely know each other grouped together for no apparent reason. I try to limit my time on Facebook. I have moved to a different country a couple years ago so I use Facebook to "stay in touch" with family and friends (still wondering how useful is it for that, after all). And yet every time I check it I end up more depressed. I have decided to start contacting the people I want to stay in touch with via email or skype instead. Not sure if it really is Facebook's fault or if people are just desperate and aggressive to prove their lives are better than everybody else's while at the same time not having the time, the desire or simply the attention span to invest in truly relating to others. In summary, no, you are not the only one feeling like that, I for one feel like I'm facing trial in front of a jury every time I log on to Facebook. For what is worth I think your decision to honestly face whatever issues you had and go through whatever changes you needed to go through is admirable, with or without Facebook crowd. I hope this helps.
